title: A Clock for the Bridge
premise: In the winter of 1899, Freya Iversen works as a nurse in a military hospital in a contested Baltic port city, secretly recording in her ledger the names of soldiers erased from official reports—men written out to protect officers' reputations. When an unknown woman leaves a six-year-old boy, Emil, at the hospital door with a note reading 'forget this face,' Freya recognizes him as the son of a soldier her ledger says never existed. Keeping Emil alive means confronting Colonel Brandt, whose career is built on those omissions, and smuggling the ledger itself across three city checkpoints before New Year's Eve, when the century—and all records of the old regime's dead—are scheduled to be burned. Freya pays dearly: a friend dies covering her escape, and she reaches the bridge at midnight with the ledger and the child, trading her own name and safety for theirs, ending the book as one of the unnamed she once recorded.
about_author: Yara Iversen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed-person records in northern European municipal collections. She writes historical fiction about the people official histories leave off the page.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Introduces the hospital ward, the war's quiet attrition, and the ledger hidden beneath floorboards where she records soldiers struck from official rolls. Establishes her rule: carry nothing you cannot run with. Emotional beat: weary vigilance.

chapters.title: What the Officers Sign
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She witnesses Colonel Brandt dictate a casualty report that erases eleven men after a failed advance. She copies their names by candlelight. Emotional beat: cold anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: A Knock After Curfew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A hooded woman leaves a shivering boy, Emil, at the door with a note: 'forget this face.' Freya hides him in the linen store as patrols pass. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into instinct.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Emil's POV, fragmentary and childlike. He remembers his father's hands, a burning farmhouse, being told not to say his surname. Emotional beat: disoriented trust beginning to form.

chapters.title: Ledger Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Freya realizes Emil's father is one of her erased names—a sergeant blamed for Brandt's blunder. The boy is living proof of the omission. Emotional beat: dread of what evidence makes her.

chapters.title: Sister Anneli's Bargain
chapters.summary: Anneli's POV. The head nurse discovers Emil and chooses silence, revealing she lost brothers to the same reports. She becomes Freya's first ally. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in shared grief.

chapters.title: Brandt Inspects the Ward
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Brandt tours the hospital; Freya must hide Emil twice in an hour while maintaining perfect composure. She notices Brandt's aide watching her too closely. Emotional beat: terror performed as calm.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Jonas's POV. A mapmaker who owes Freya for treating his daughter offers his knowledge of checkpoint schedules—the bridge, the customs house, the garrison gate. Emotional beat: reluctant courage.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: Freya decodes the note left with Emil: it matches handwriting in an old discharge file, pointing to the mother's identity and her flight toward the coast. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Winter Rations
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Food runs short; the ward shares everything. Emil learns to fold bandages and earns his place among the wounded men. Emotional beat: fragile domestic warmth.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A test run: she carries medicine past the garrison gate, memorizing which guards take bribes and which take pride. Emotional beat: measured confidence.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: A dying soldier murmurs the erased sergeant's name; an orderly reports it. Brandt orders a search of staff quarters. Emotional beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The search comes; Freya buries the ledger in coal dust and sits on Emil's hiding place, lying to Brandt's face for the first time. Emotional beat: the point of no return crossed.

chapters.title: Anneli's Confession
chapters.summary: Anneli reveals she once reported a colleague to survive, and vows this time to stand the other way. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: The Customs House Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonas maps the second checkpoint and warns that after New Year's Eve, all old-regime records burn—including anything that could clear Emil's father. Emotional beat: urgency made concrete.

chapters.title: Emil Learns His Father's Name
chapters.summary: Emil's POV. Freya tells him his father was a good soldier, wrongly blamed. He practices writing the name until it fills a page. Emotional beat: grief transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Aide's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt's aide, Lieutenant Kessler, privately offers Freya passage in exchange for the ledger—he wants leverage over Brandt. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a helpful face.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Freya sorts her life into one bag: the ledger, Emil's boots, her mother's ring. Everything else goes to the ward. Emotional beat: the theme made physical.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Laundry
chapters.summary: An orderly sells information about 'the nurse and the boy.' Freya learns the search will resume after Christmas. Emotional beat: paranoia invading sanctuary.

chapters.title: Christmas in the Linen Store
chapters.summary: The ward stages a secret holiday for Emil—candle stubs, a carved wooden horse from a one-armed patient. Emotional beat: joy stolen back from scarcity.

chapters.title: Kessler's Price Rises
chapters.summary: Kessler demands the original ledger plus Freya's silence about his role. She realizes he'd bury the truth as thoroughly as Brandt. Emotional beat: disillusionment.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Freya smuggles copied pages sewn into a blanket through the customs house, but a guard's suspicion forces her to abandon half the copies. Emotional beat: costly partial victory.

chapters.title: Anneli Covers the Ward
chapters.summary: Anneli's POV. She falsifies a quarantine notice to buy Freya three days, knowing it may cost her post—or worse. Emotional beat: sacrifice accepted without drama.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Freya scouts the final checkpoint, the old bridge, and meets the ferryman who owes Jonas a debt. He agrees to wait one night only. Emotional beat: hope balanced on a single night.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV, chillingly bureaucratic. He orders the ward sealed and the century-burning moved up a day. Emotional beat: evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: Running Out of Century
chapters.summary: Freya learns the bonfire date changed. Every plan collapses into a single impossible evening. Emotional beat: vertigo of compressed time.

chapters.title: The Quarantine Breaks
chapters.summary: Soldiers storm the ward; Anneli burns her own false papers to draw them off and is arrested. Freya escapes with Emil through the coal chute. Emotional beat: heartbreak as fuel.

chapters.title: Through the Frozen Streets
chapters.summary: Freya and Emil flee through curfewed alleys, hiding in a burned chapel where Emil finds his father's regimental tag among relics. Emotional beat: grief and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Kessler's Last Gambit
chapters.summary: Kessler intercepts them, demanding the ledger again; Freya gives him the decoy copy she prepared, keeping the true one against her ribs. Emotional beat: cunning under exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Patience Ends
chapters.summary: They reach the river too late—the ferryman is gone. Freya must attempt the bridge checkpoints on foot with minutes to midnight. Emotional beat: despair refused.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Gate
chapters.summary: Freya uses the bribed guard's routine, walking Emil through as her nephew, pulse hammering. Emotional beat: terror choreographed into performance.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Bridgehead
chapters.summary: The suspicious guard from earlier recognizes her blanket. A wounded patient she once saved, now on sentry duty, vouches for her at terrible risk. Emotional beat: debts repaid in kind.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Toll House
chapters.summary: Brandt himself waits at the toll house, having guessed her route. He offers her freedom for the ledger and the boy's silence. Emotional beat: corruption offering its gentlest face.

chapters.title: Midnight on the Bridge
chapters.summary: Climax. Freya refuses; Brandt seizes the ledger bag—but it holds the decoy. Church bells begin striking the new century as she and Emil slip past in the crowd of revelers crossing to the fireworks. Emotional beat: triumph inside chaos.

chapters.title: The Bonfire Across the Water
chapters.summary: From the far bank they watch the old records burn, the true ledger safe in Freya's coat. Somewhere in the flames go the lies; somewhere in her coat, the truth. Emotional beat: exhale after drowning.

chapters.title: What Anneli Paid
chapters.summary: News reaches them: Anneli faces trial but survives, her sentence softened when Freya mails copied pages to a newspaper editor. Emotional beat: justice as slow seed.

chapters.title: A Face Worth Remembering
chapters.summary: Freya and Emil reach the coast; the mother's trail ends at a convent that takes children in. Freya must decide whether to leave him or stay. Emotional beat: belonging weighed against safety.

chapters.title: The Choice to Be Named
chapters.summary: Freya signs the convent register—not anonymously, but with her full name, the first time she claims it in years. She stays as the infirmary nurse. Emotional beat: invisibility voluntarily ended.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Spring. The published excerpts force an inquiry; the erased sergeant's name is restored posthumously, and Emil speaks it at a small memorial. Emotional beat: mourning given its dignity back.

chapters.title: A Clock for the Bridge
chapters.summary: Years later, Emil, now grown, visits the bridge clock that still keeps imperfect time. Freya, older, adds a final line to the ledger: her own name, freely given. Emotional beat: peace earned, memory kept.
